Spec 16 Bug Fixes, the author's reports (#33) — semantic diff

Branch feature/godot-mvpBase e175dfe (Stage log: pull request opened (#27))Head ccf39a1 Target mainDate 2026-11-22 Commits 6Files 28 · +1342 / −671 Written by REVIEW: + CODE REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

The second round of spec 16 answers three reports of the author after the first close: the desktop run offered a QR scan that can only fail, there was no way to shoot with the keyboard, and no screen said how to play. Range e175dfe..ccf39a1 — this run's commits only (the plan commit 33fc2c7 and Steps 6–10); the first round has its own page.

  • Outside the web export Scan QR code is disabled and a hint says to use the browser version or type the code; the README says how to scan on this computer (localhost:8060).
  • Space (a new shoot action) fires at the nearest target in range or straight ahead, held for auto-fire; a mouse click no longer fires; Back cannot take focus, so Space never leaves the arena.
  • The Info page starts with "How to play" (five sections from one source, ControlsHelp, with the numbers read from the rules), and Training and a match show a controls hint that fades after 5 s.
  • 402 of 402 tests pass and lint is clean (re-run by the review); server/ and ui/ are unchanged.
  • Five findings, none Blocking: Step 10 dropped test_save_tabs.gd from the architecture's test list, the spec's Stage log is broken by lone CR line breaks, and the touch position of the start hint is untested.

Recommendation: Approve with follow-ups — no Blocking finding; findings 1–5 to fix now.

The second round of spec 16 disables the scan where it cannot work with a hint, makes Space the shot (the mouse no longer fires), adds "How to play" to the Info page and a controls hint at the start of Training and a match.

Author Q&A

Why is Scan QR code not made to work in the desktop run?
D10: Godot 4.7's CameraServer has no camera feed on Windows, and the game's scanner is the browser's (web/qr_scanner.js); a desktop QR decoder would be a new dependency for a run the kids do not use. The README says how to scan on this computer (localhost:8060).
Why does Space aim at the nearest target and not where the fighter looks?
D11: the same rule as the quick tap on the right stick (_aim_direction, nearest of tap_targets() within Combat.SHOT_RANGE, else straight ahead), so the keyboard and touch aim alike and a kid does not need a mouse to aim.
Why "How to play" on the Info page and not a new screen?
D14: one tap from home, no new home button, the five home layouts unchanged; the start hint points to it ("More in Info").
Where does the start hint stand on a touch screen?
288 px above the bottom edge, clear of the sticks (Step 9 Notes); it was not seen on a screenshot and has no test (this computer has no touch screen) - see finding 3.

This range does not touch that code. The same kind of slip as finding 5 is back (finding 5 here), and Step 10's documentation edit removed a line the first round wrote (finding 1).

Highlights

1 · Space fires while it is held

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.gd:95-102 · e35e8aa · Step 7 · S28, D11

95func _process(delta: float) -> void:
97 _camera_target, _wanted_camera_target(), delta, CAMERA_FOLLOW_RATE
98 )
99 _place_camera()
78 if _mouse_held:
79 _fire_at_mouse()
100 if read_player_input and Input.is_action_pressed("shoot"):
101 fire(_aim_direction())
102 _update_aim_line()

What changed: The mouse-held branch is replaced: every frame, while the shoot action is held and the player's input is read, the arena fires at _aim_direction().

Why it matters: This is the whole keyboard shooting path; the rate and the countdown / end lock come from fire() (cool-down in fire_from, player_can_act()).

What to check: Holding Space does not fire faster than Combat.COOLDOWN (test_arena_space), and nothing fires during the countdown or after the end (test_match_arena).

Concepts: Input.is_action_pressedPolls whether any event of an input action is held right now; polling in _process gives held-key auto-fire without key-repeat events, and the cool-down in fire() sets the rate. read_player_inputThe arena's switch for reading the player's keys and sticks; tests turn it off and on, and Space obeys it like the movement keys. _processCalled every rendered frame with the time since the last one; here it moves the camera and fires while Space is held.

2 · The start hint and its fade

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.gd:74-92 · 9fdc7ef · Step 9 · S31, D15

74 _update_fps_label()
75 _show_controls_hint()
76
77
78func _show_controls_hint() -> void:
79 var lines: Array[String] = [ControlsHelp.KEYBOARD_HINT]
80 if DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available():
81 lines.append(ControlsHelp.TOUCH_HINT)
82 # The sticks stand at the bottom corners; the hint goes above their height.
83 _controls_hint.offset_top = -HINT_ABOVE_STICKS - 104.0
84 _controls_hint.offset_bottom = -HINT_ABOVE_STICKS
85 lines.append(ControlsHelp.MORE_IN_INFO)
86 _controls_hint.text = "\n".join(lines)
87 _controls_hint.modulate.a = 1.0
88 _controls_hint.show()
89 var fade: Tween = create_tween()
90 fade.tween_interval(HINT_SECONDS)
91 fade.tween_property(_controls_hint, "modulate:a", 0.0, HINT_FADE_SECONDS)
92 fade.tween_callback(_controls_hint.hide)

What changed: _ready shows ControlsHint with the keyboard line, the touch line on a touch screen (and moves it above the sticks), then "More in Info"; a tween waits HINT_SECONDS, fades the alpha over HINT_FADE_SECONDS and hides it.

Why it matters: The touch branch is where the kids play (iPad, phone) and is the one part not tested or seen (finding 3); the -104.0 is the label's assumed height.

What to check: At 844×390 on a touch screen the hint spans y 258–362 of the 650-high content and the countdown 135–255; a fourth line (a wrap) would grow it upwards into the countdown.

Concepts: TweenGodot 4's create_tween() animates properties over time and runs callbacks in sequence; here: a pause, the fade of modulate:a, then hide(). modulate:aThe alpha of a CanvasItem's modulate colour, applied to the node and its children; fading it to 0 makes the label vanish smoothly. DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_availableTrue when the platform reports a touch screen (a phone, an iPad, a touch laptop); the sticks use the same check, so the hint follows the sticks. offset_top / offset_bottomWith anchors at the bottom (1.0), negative offsets place the label that many pixels above the bottom edge of the HUD.

207## A quick tap fires at the nearest of `tap_targets` in range, else straight ahead.
208func _tap_direction() -> Vector2:

What changed: _fire_at_mouse is removed and _tap_direction becomes _aim_direction, used by the stick's quick tap and by Space.

Why it matters: One rule for the nearest target in range (Combat.nearest_target over tap_targets(), the live bots in a match, the standing dummies in Training).

What to check: tap_targets() is overridden by MatchArena so Space never aims at a knocked-out bot (test_space_fires_at_the_nearest_bot_and_nothing_after_the_end).

Concepts: Combat.nearest_targetA pure rule that returns the index of the nearest point within a range, or -1; the arena turns it into a direction. Virtual method overrideMatchArena redefines tap_targets(); Arena calls it without knowing which scene it is, so Training and a match share _aim_direction.

4 · The mouse input is gone

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.gd:123-127 · e35e8aa · Step 7 · S29, D12

104## The mouse aims and fires; GUI controls (Back) take their clicks before this, and mouse
105## events made from touches are ignored, so a touch never fires twice.
106func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
107 if event is InputEventMouse and event.device == InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_EMULATION:
108 return
109 if event is InputEventMouseMotion:
110 _mouse_position = (event as InputEventMouseMotion).position
111 elif event is InputEventMouseButton:
112 var button: InputEventMouseButton = event
113 if button.button_index != MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
114 return
115 _mouse_held = button.pressed
116 _mouse_position = button.position
117 if button.pressed:

126## Fires a shot along `direction` (ground plane, x and z) when the cool-down is over: the
127## fighter turns that way and recoils, the shot leaves the muzzle. True when it fired.

What changed: The whole _unhandled_input (mouse motion, left button held, ignoring emulated mouse from touch) is removed.

Why it matters: A click now fires nothing; Back still takes its click as a GUI control, and touch goes through the sticks only.

What to check: test_an_emulated_mouse_click_does_not_fire and the new click test pass; the record block space-shoots shows 1 shot before and 0 after for the same click.

Concepts: _unhandled_inputReceives input events that no GUI control consumed; removing it means mouse events reach no game code in the arena. DEVICE_ID_EMULATIONThe device id Godot gives mouse events it makes from touches; the removed code skipped them so a touch never fired twice.

5 · Back cannot be pressed with Space

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.tscn:70-74 · e35e8aa · Step 7 · S28, D11

70[node name="Hud" type="CanvasLayer" parent="."]
71

73focus_mode = 0

What changed: The arena's BackButton gets focus_mode = 0 (FOCUS_NONE).

Why it matters: Space is also ui_accept; a focused Back would leave the match when the player shoots. A button without focus can still be clicked or touched.

What to check: The record block input-map and the probe: grab_focus() on Back succeeds before and fails after.

Concepts: focus_modeWhether a Control can take keyboard focus: FOCUS_NONE (0), FOCUS_CLICK (1) or FOCUS_ALL (2, a Button's default). ui_acceptThe built-in action (Enter, Space) that presses the focused button; with no focusable button in the arena it does nothing there.

Concepts glossary

Input.is_action_pressed
Polls whether any event of an input action is held right now; polling in _process gives held-key auto-fire without key-repeat events, and the cool-down in fire() sets the rate.
read_player_input
The arena's switch for reading the player's keys and sticks; tests turn it off and on, and Space obeys it like the movement keys.
_process
Called every rendered frame with the time since the last one; here it moves the camera and fires while Space is held.
Tween
Godot 4's create_tween() animates properties over time and runs callbacks in sequence; here: a pause, the fade of modulate:a, then hide().
modulate:a
The alpha of a CanvasItem's modulate colour, applied to the node and its children; fading it to 0 makes the label vanish smoothly.
DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available
True when the platform reports a touch screen (a phone, an iPad, a touch laptop); the sticks use the same check, so the hint follows the sticks.
offset_top / offset_bottom
With anchors at the bottom (1.0), negative offsets place the label that many pixels above the bottom edge of the HUD.
Combat.nearest_target
A pure rule that returns the index of the nearest point within a range, or -1; the arena turns it into a direction.
Virtual method override
MatchArena redefines tap_targets(); Arena calls it without knowing which scene it is, so Training and a match share _aim_direction.
_unhandled_input
Receives input events that no GUI control consumed; removing it means mouse events reach no game code in the arena.
DEVICE_ID_EMULATION
The device id Godot gives mouse events it makes from touches; the removed code skipped them so a touch never fired twice.
focus_mode
Whether a Control can take keyboard focus: FOCUS_NONE (0), FOCUS_CLICK (1) or FOCUS_ALL (2, a Button's default).
ui_accept
The built-in action (Enter, Space) that presses the focused button; with no focusable button in the arena it does nothing there.
mouse_filter = 2
MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE: the control never receives or stops mouse and touch events, so the sticks under it still work.
grow_vertical = 0
GROW_DIRECTION_BEGIN: when the text needs more height than the offsets give, the label grows upwards, away from the bottom edge.
Inherited scene
match.tscn instances arena.tscn as its root and adds to it; nodes added to the arena scene appear in the match too.
Member initialiser
A var with a default runs when the object is created, before _ready, so a caller can override it between instantiate() and add_child().
add_theme_color_override
Sets one theme colour on this control only; here the hint uses the screen's MESSAGE_COLOR without a new theme entry.
OS.has_feature("web")
True in a web export running in a browser; a feature tag known at run time, so the same script decides per build.
static func
A function of the class, called without an instance (QrScanner.can_scan()); the hack screen asks before any scanner exists.
validate_node_name
Returns the string with characters a node name cannot hold replaced; the rows are named after their title so tests can find them.
theme_type_variation
Selects a named variation of a theme type (SubheadingLabel, WordLabel) so the page uses the shared theme and adds no colours or fonts.
String % formatting
GDScript's printf-style operator: "%d" % value; with an Array for several values; here it keeps the help true when a rule changes.
RefCounted pure class
A class with only static functions and constants, no node; the help is testable without a scene like Vocabulary.
physical_keycode
The key's position on a US layout, independent of the user's keyboard language; Space is 32 everywhere.
Input map
The project's named actions and their events (project.godot [input]); code asks for the action, never for a key.
Architecture document
docs/architecture.md says where each part of the Godot game lives and which tests cover it; S32 asks to update it, not to lose earlier entries.
Word-level diff
A one-line paragraph changed in place hides removals; git diff --word-diff shows the deleted words of the long line.
